Not to jump right to Hitler, but it kind of hints at my point. Ideas can absolutely be dangerous. Viewing any human as subhuman is inherently dangerous. Maybe I should elaborate.

There is nothing wrong with the "idea" that certain people are subhuman. Personally I don't agree with this particular idea, but if you are so afraid of this idea that you cannot even hold it in your head for one second because you think it is "evil" or "dangerous," you begin to tread a dark path. I forget who it was, but someone once said that the mark of being a truly logical skeptic is the ability to hold an idea you don't agree with in your head and explore it without prejudice. Why is this important? Because you cannot guarantee that everything you currently believe or think is in fact true; everybody is wrong about something at one time or another, even if we don't like to admit it. Once you close your mind off to certain things you de facto decrease your ability to find the truth.

If you're still not convinced, think about all sorts of ideas that were considered "dangerous" in the past:

"Cannabis is okay to enjoy in moderation"

"People of different races should be allowed to mix"

"The earth is not the center of the universe"

"The sovereign is not always right"

These ideas were all considered dangerous among the majority of certain populations at certain periods in human history. When you embrace orthodoxy and shut off your brain at what is considered taboo within the society you inhabit, you cripple yourself. Do you honestly think that there are not some hidden orthodoxies in our current society that humans 200 years from now will look back on and shake their heads? Given how human civilization has evolved, I would be surprised if there were not.
